headline: Iran says two more tankers hit mines at Hormuz as talks on reopening it continue and Brent hovers near $110. Cyclone Murasu nears India's east coast, and Russia launched 759 drones at Ukraine on 1 Nov.

situations.name: US–Iran war and Gulf energy shock
situations.summary: Iran says two tankers hit mines at Hormuz on 1 Nov after attacks on 30–31 Oct; Brent near $110, TTF above €100; reopening talks go on.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine war and NATO's flank
situations.summary: 759 Russian drones launched on 1 Nov in two waves, cutting power to hundreds of thousands; drones closed Jersey airspace on 30–31 Oct.

situations.name: Super El Niño
situations.summary: ONI +2.2: drought in Australia and East Africa, record warmth and weaker carbon sinks.

situations.name: Ebola outbreak, DR Congo
situations.summary: 10,141 cases and 4,928 deaths in DR Congo to 27 Oct (ECDC), with cases in Kenya and Nigeria; a WHO emergency (PHEIC) since May.

situations.name: Sudan war
situations.summary: Record drone attacks on civilians in October; the army rejects talks; famine confirmed in 2025.

situations.name: Cyclone Murasu
situations.summary: Severe cyclonic storm due to cross south Andhra Pradesh overnight 2–3 Nov, gusts to 120km/h; GDACS lowered its alert to green on 2 Nov.

situations.name: France: debt stress and protests
situations.summary: OAT–Bund spread near 160bp; mass social protests for a third weekend, spreading to Germany.

situations.name: Energy shock feeding inflation
situations.summary: US CPI at 4.0% on the oil shock; a Bank of England rise to 4% widely expected on 5 Nov; Egypt hiked on 29 Oct.

situations.name: Record Binance hack attributed to North Korea
situations.summary: About $6.3bn drained from Binance in late October; FBI blamed North Korea on 1 Nov; withdrawals resuming since 31 Oct.

signals.name: US equity stress
signals.summary: VIX just under 20 and S&P 500 3% off its high before the 3 Nov midterms
signals.state: At the 30 Oct close the S&P 500 stood about 3% below its 52-week high and the VIX was 19.4, just under the 20 Watch line; US trading resumes on 2 Nov. The 3 Nov US midterms, the 5 Nov Bank of England decision and 6 Nov US payrolls fall this week.
signals.for_you: Share prices are moving within normal ranges. Pension and investment values may swing more around this week's elections and central bank decisions.
signals.rubric_hit: VIX 19.4 < 20 Watch line; S&P drawdown 3% < 10%

signals.state: The FTSE 100 last closed on 30 Oct at 10,730, about 1.7% below its 52-week high; London reopens on 2 Nov. Its heavy weighting to oil, gas and mining firms has cushioned it from the energy shock. The Bank of England decides on rates on 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: UK shares are near record levels. Pension funds with UK equity exposure have not seen a market fall of note.

signals.name: Crypto stress
signals.summary: Binance reopening after record $6.3bn hack; Bitcoin 10% off its high
signals.state: Binance, the largest exchange, began resuming withdrawals on 31 Oct after about $6.3bn was drained in late October, saying about 90% of stolen user assets are covered (CNBC). The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea on 1 Nov. Bitcoin was near $78,200 early on 2 Nov, about 10% below its high; the exchange's promised proof of reserves is the next marker.
signals.for_you: Binance customers may still face delays on some withdrawals. Any shortfall in reserves would matter most for those holding funds on the exchange.
signals.rubric_hit: Top-10 exchange under stress (Binance hack, phased withdrawals) = Watch; BTC drawdown 10% < 25%

signals.name: Dollar funding stress
signals.summary: US overnight funding calm: SOFR within 5bp of IORB, no Fed repo use
signals.state: The secured overnight financing rate (SOFR) peaked 5bp above the Fed's interest on reserves over the five days to 29 Oct, inside the 10bp Watch line, and Fed standing repo operations were near zero to 30 Oct. Money markets show no sign of a dollar shortage.
signals.for_you: Short-term dollar funding markets that banks rely on are working normally.
signals.rubric_hit: SOFR–IORB 5d max 5bp < 10bp; repo ops < $15bn

signals.name: Private credit stress
signals.value: Q3 exits 11.5% of NAV vs 5% caps
signals.summary: Big private credit funds still capping withdrawals, though Q3 requests eased
signals.state: In Q3, 19 non-traded BDCs received redemption requests worth $13.8bn, 11.5% of NAV, and met about 40%, leaving $8.2bn unmet (Stanger, 2 Oct). Blackstone's BCRED held repurchases to its 5% cap against requests of about $4.3bn, roughly 10% of shares. Requests eased from 12.7% in Q2, and Stanger said demand may have peaked.
signals.for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may not be able to withdraw all their money when they ask. Effects so far are confined to fund investors.
signals.rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions (BCRED at 5% cap) = Watch

signals.name: US inflation
signals.summary: US CPI at 4.0%, pushed up by the oil shock
signals.state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7% in August, as energy prices fed through, within the 3–4.5% Watch band. The Fed raised rates in September and held on 28 Oct, with markets pricing another hike in December. October CPI is due mid-November.
signals.for_you: Higher US inflation keeps global interest rates elevated, which affects borrowing costs well beyond the US.
signals.rubric_hit: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.summary: Euro area grew 0.4% in Q3, but France contracted and October PMIs slowed
signals.state: Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct showed euro-area GDP up 0.4% in Q3, though French output contracted. October flash PMIs (23 Oct) showed expansion weakening, and the ECB warned on 29 Oct that energy prices pose downside risks to growth. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI is yet confirmed.
signals.for_you: Europe is still growing, but the energy shock is beginning to bite. A slowdown there would weigh on UK exports.
signals.rubric_hit: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.

signals.name: China economy
signals.summary: China's factory PMI slipped to 49.3 in October after 4.5% Q3 growth
signals.state: The official NBS manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, below the 50.0 consensus (released 31 Oct), and services also contracted. Q3 GDP grew 4.5% year on year, within the official range, so growth is not yet clearly below target and there is no sign of financial contagion.
signals.for_you: China is not currently a source of global shock, though weak domestic demand keeps it reliant on exports and trade relations.
signals.rubric_hit: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.

signals.name: Central bank stress
signals.summary: Central banks caught between energy-driven inflation and slowing growth
signals.state: The Fed hiked to 3.75–4% in September and held on 28 Oct in a 10–2 vote; the ECB held at 2.50% on 29 Oct, warning of upside inflation and downside growth risks. The Bank of England decides on 5 Nov, with a hike widely expected. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma across the G7.
signals.for_you: Interest rates are more likely to rise than fall in the near term in the US and UK, which affects mortgages, loans and savings rates.
signals.rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.

signals.name: Sovereign debt stress
signals.summary: French borrowing costs spike: OAT–Bund spread near 160bp
signals.state: France's 10-year spread over German Bunds was about 159bp on 30 Oct, above the 150bp Alert line, after peaking above 170bp on 22 Oct (Teleborsa). French GDP contracted in Q3 and street protests entered a third weekend on 31 Oct. UK 30-year gilts are near 5.7%.
signals.for_you: Rising government borrowing costs tend to feed into mortgage and business lending rates, and can force tax rises or spending cuts.
signals.rubric_hit: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.

signals.summary: Global PMI strong in September, but October flashes and China's PMI softened
signals.state: The J.P.Morgan Global Composite PMI rose in September to its joint-highest level since 2021 (published 6 Oct). October readings so far point to softer momentum: euro-area flashes slowed (23 Oct) and China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 (31 Oct). The October global figures are due 2–4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Global activity has held up well so far despite the energy shock.
signals.rubric_hit: J.P.Morgan Global Composite PMI > 51.

signals.state: Initial US jobless claims were 194,000 in the week to 24 Oct, taking the four-week average to about 197,000, level with its 52-week low and far from the 15% Watch line. Layoffs show no sign of rising despite higher energy costs.
signals.for_you: The US jobs market remains tight, with no wave of layoffs under way.

signals.name: Emerging-market stress
signals.summary: Pressure on oil importers such as Egypt, but no emerging-market crisis
signals.state: The Egyptian pound passed 56 per dollar at the central bank on 26 Oct, a record low, and Egypt unexpectedly raised rates by one point to 20% on 29 Oct, citing energy prices (Rio Times). Indonesia has repeatedly intervened for the rupiah this year. No major emerging economy has defaulted, imposed capital controls or lost more than 10% in a month as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Oil-importing emerging economies are under strain from the energy shock. People with ties to Egypt may see further moves in the exchange rate.
signals.rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month or emergency IMF request

signals.summary: Brent near $110 as Iran reports more tankers hit at Hormuz
signals.state: Brent traded near $109.7 early on 2 Nov, just under the $110 Alert line but up 9% over the month, and remains at Alert under the board's hysteresis rule. Iran's IRGC said two tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 Nov, while talks on a two-day plan to reopen the strait continue.
signals.for_you: Expect continued high petrol, diesel and heating-oil prices, with knock-on effects on transport costs and inflation.
signals.rubric_hit: Brent $109.7 near $110 Alert line; Hormuz largely shut

signals.summary: European gas above €100/MWh with Gulf LNG routes still blocked
signals.state: Dutch TTF gas last traded near €103/MWh on 30 Oct, above the Alert line and up 38% over the month. signals.for_you: Wholesale gas is feeding into energy bills; the Ofgem price cap sets what most UK households pay. Ofgem and gov.uk list help for those struggling with bills.

This follows tanker attacks on 30–31 Oct. Drones hit at least seven cargo ships off Romania and Bulgaria in October.

signals.summary: Container rates above $4,400/FEU despite a 3% weekly fall
signals.state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 3% to $4,429 per 40ft container on 29 Oct, still above the $4,000 Alert line; Shanghai–Los Angeles was $7,514 and Shanghai–New York $9,631. Gulf disruption and rerouting keep capacity tight. The next WCI reading is due 5 Nov.
signals.for_you: High shipping costs typically feed into prices of imported goods with a lag of a few months.

signals.name: Global food prices
signals.summary: FAO food index at 136, up 5.8% on a year
signals.state: The FAO Food Price Index rose 1.5% in September to 136.0, 5.8% above a year earlier and above the 135 Alert line (published 8 Oct). Cereals rose 5.1% and sugar 6.1%, driven by Black Sea logistics, dry weather and Hormuz shipping uncertainty. The October figure is due in the first week of November.
signals.for_you: Food inflation is likely to stay elevated. Import-dependent poorer countries are most exposed.
signals.rubric_hit: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.

signals.name: Critical minerals
signals.summary: China's rare-earth export pause expires 10 Nov; helium squeeze persists
signals.state: China's suspension of some rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, with no renewal announced as of late October. The loss of Qatari helium through Hormuz, plus China's July helium export ban, has created shortages for chipmakers; the US has designated helium a critical material. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed.
signals.for_you: Shortages of specialist materials can raise costs and delay electronics, vehicles and defence equipment.
signals.rubric_hit: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.

signals.name: Fertiliser supply
signals.summary: Hormuz closure has stranded Gulf urea exports; prices up but below April peak
signals.state: No non-Iranian granular urea has cleared Hormuz since mid-October, and Argus counts at least 21 vessels with 919,000 tonnes of urea held in the Gulf, against normal exports of about 1Mt a month (28 Oct). Middle East urea was $447.50/t on 27 Oct, well below the April peak of about $780.
signals.for_you: Higher fertiliser costs tend to feed into food prices over the following seasons, hitting import-dependent farmers and poorer countries first.
signals.rubric_hit: Key export route (Hormuz) closed to Gulf urea = Alert

signals.name: Nuclear plant safety
signals.summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on one power line as strikes on Ukraine's grid continue
signals.state: Zaporizhzhia lost its last off-site line on 20 Aug, its 26th such loss, and ran on diesel for about 18 days until an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire allowed repairs (ANS). It still depends on a single 330kV line while Russian strikes on Ukraine's grid continue (1 Nov). Trump has raised further bombing of Iranian nuclear sites (Al Jazeera, 1 Nov).
signals.for_you: No radiological release has been reported. Official guidance in an emergency would come from the IAEA and national authorities.
signals.rubric_hit: IAEA-reported loss of all off-site power (Aug–Sep); plant still on one line

The Lindsey Graham Act, signed in October, expands secondary sanctions on Russia's trading partners. No new major package was announced to 1 Nov.

signals.name: Russia–Ukraine
signals.summary: Two waves totalling 759 drones on 1 Nov hit energy sites; Ukraine strikes Russian plants
signals.state: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 433 drones overnight into 1 Nov and 326 more during the day, hitting energy sites in four regions and leaving hundreds of thousands of households without power. signals.value: WFP Gaza aid cut for 500k (19 Oct)
signals.summary: Funding gaps force WFP ration cuts in Gaza and the West Bank
signals.state: WFP said on 19 Oct it would cut monthly food aid in Gaza from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people and halve family rations, after receiving less than half its usual Palestine funding in 2026; it needs $450m for six months. West Bank aid was halved in September (Al Jazeera).
signals.for_you: Funding shortfalls reduce aid in crisis zones. OCHA and ReliefWeb publish appeal details.
signals.rubric_hit: Major ration cuts announced = Watch

sources.title: Al Jazeera — WFP cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza amid funding shortages

signals.name: UK inflation & rates
signals.summary: UK CPI 3.5% and a Bank of England rate rise expected on 5 Nov
signals.state: UK CPI inflation rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1%. Bank Rate is 3.75%, and money markets almost fully price a rise at the 5 Nov meeting, with further increases priced for February and July (Trading Economics, 30 Oct).
signals.for_you: Mortgage rates are more likely to rise than fall in the coming months. Savings rates may also edge up.
signals.rubric_hit: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK 10-year gilt yield and BoE expectations

signals.name: Gilt market
signals.summary: Gilt yields near 19-year highs ahead of an expected 5 Nov rate rise
signals.state: The 10-year gilt yield fell below 5.3% on 29–30 Oct, its lowest since 22 Sep but still near 19-year highs and about 86bp higher than a year ago (Trading Economics). Money markets almost fully price a Bank Rate rise on 5 Nov and further increases in 2027. Auctions have been orderly.
signals.for_you: Fixed-rate mortgage and loan pricing follows gilt and swap rates, so new deals stay expensive.
signals.rubric_hit: Gilt yields near multi-decade highs = Watch; 10y 1m move −13bp

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields fall to one-month lows

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.summary: Energy price cap forecast to rise about 25% in January
signals.state: The Ofgem cap for October to December is £1,723 a year for a typical dual-fuel household. Uswitch's average of British Gas, EDF and E.ON forecasts (updated 30 Oct) points to a 27% rise in January 2027, above the 20% Alert line, driven by the wholesale gas surge. Ofgem announces the January cap by 25 Nov.
signals.for_you: Household energy bills are likely to rise sharply from 1 January. Ofgem and Citizens Advice publish guidance on support if you're struggling to pay.
signals.rubric_hit: Cap > £2,200, or forecast rise ≥ 20%.

signals.name: NHS & respiratory
signals.summary: Flu, COVID and RSV at low or baseline levels; flu usually rises in November
signals.state: UKHSA's 29 Oct update (week 43) showed flu stable at low levels (6.6% positivity), COVID low and falling (8.3%), and RSV rising but at baseline. UKHSA notes flu usually picks up in November; the next update is due 5 Nov. Resident doctors in England strike from 14 to 19 Nov.
signals.for_you: If eligible, get your flu and COVID vaccines before winter. Use NHS 111 for urgent but non-emergency care.
signals.rubric_hit: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.

signals.name: UK terrorism threat level
signals.summary: UK terrorism threat level raised to Severe: an attack is highly likely
signals.state: The UK national terrorism threat level remains Severe, meaning an attack is highly likely, after MI5 raised it in October 2026. The MI5 Director General warned on 13 Oct of a rising threat from anti-migrant and anti-Muslim extremism alongside Islamist terrorism. No change as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Stay alert in crowded places and report anything suspicious via gov.uk/ACT or 999 in an emergency. Follow police and MI5 guidance.
signals.rubric_hit: Severe or Critical.

signals.name: UK strikes & disruption
signals.summary: Resident doctors strike 14–19 Nov; consultants plan two days
signals.state: The BMA has called a six-day strike by resident doctors in England from 14 to 19 Nov, and consultants have announced a two-day strike in November (NHS Employers). These are strikes in one sector, within the Watch band. No national infrastructure failure was reported as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: Attend appointments unless told otherwise. The NHS will contact you if yours is rescheduled. Use 111 or 999 as usual.
signals.rubric_hit: National strike in one sector or major infrastructure disruption.

signals.name: GB energy supply margins
signals.summary: GB gas and power margins adequate for winter; no notices issued
signals.state: National Gas said on 23 Oct that GB has enough supply capability (592 mcm/d) to meet 1-in-20 peak demand of 493 mcm/d this winter. NESO's early view forecast a 5.5GW de-rated electricity margin, with some tight days likely in January. No margin notices had been issued as of 1 Nov.
signals.for_you: No sign of supply interruptions to UK homes; the main pressure is on prices, not availability.
signals.rubric_hit: Adequate margins; no notices issued
